paper_metadata.title: Automating Biomedical Knowledge Graph Construction For Context-Aware Scientific Inference

evidence.excerpt: bioRxiv preprint doi: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.01.14.699420

paper_metadata.abstract: Biomedical interactions are inherently dynamic, often shifting or even reversing under specific physiological states. Existing extraction methods simplify these mechanisms into context-agnostic binary associations, resulting in semantic loss and contradictory evidence. AutoBioKG is an end-to-end framework for context-aware biomedical knowledge graph construction using composite triplets to encode environmental conditions and entity attributes alongside core relationships. A self-evolving open information extraction model is trained on the curated BioOpenIE dataset. AutoBioKG surpasses state-of-the-art large language models in zero-shot settings on DDI, ChemProt, and BioRED, and graphs constructed by AutoBioKG outperform existing approaches on BioASQ biomedical question answering, especially for context-sensitive queries.

problem_addressed: The paper addresses semantic loss and contradictory evidence caused by representing biomedical interactions as flat, context-agnostic subject-predicate-object triples. It aims to automate extraction, normalization, knowledge fusion, and graph construction from unstructured biomedical literature while preserving entity attributes and the conditions under which relationships hold.

methodology.description: AutoBioKG uses a LLaMA3.1-8B decoder-only Transformer adapted with LoRA. It generates composite triples of the form (Subject:[Attribute], Relation:[Condition], Object:[Attribute]). A seed model is supervised-fine-tuned on BioOpenIE, then refined once using pseudo-labels from unlabeled PubMed introductions filtered jointly by token confidence and entropy. Extracted entities are normalized to UMLS concepts using candidate retrieval and SapBERT disambiguation; relations are aligned to a dynamic vocabulary using BGE-m3 similarity or added as new relation types. Verified triples are stored in Neo4j, and AutoBioKGAgent exposes extraction, normalization, graph construction, and querying through a natural-language/MCP interface.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The core representation is a schema-guided composite triple with optional subject attributes, relation conditions, and object attributes. Entity recognition is constrained by 23 UMLS semantic types; entity normalization uses UMLS Concept Unique Identifiers; the initial relation vocabulary is derived from the UMLS Semantic Network and can expand dynamically.

input_output.input_type: Unstructured biomedical research literature, including PubMed articles, abstracts, introductions, and full-text articles.
input_output.input_granularity: Document and paragraph/sentence level: introductions are segmented into 3–5 semantic paragraphs for annotation, while the final system processes document collections associated with BioASQ questions.
input_output.output_representation: Context-aware composite triples, normalized biomedical entities and relations, and a Neo4j knowledge graph containing nodes, edges, attributes, relationship conditions, and provenance/context information.

datasets: BioOpenIE: 5,129 validated composite triples from 500 biomedical research articles; 300 articles for training and 200 for testing
DDI: 1,025 documents from DrugBank and MedLine with drug-drug interaction annotations
ChemProt: 1,820 PubMed abstracts with chemical-protein interaction annotations
BioRED: biomedical entity-relation extraction corpus from PubMed abstracts
BioASQ Task 12b (2024): 5,046 training questions; filtered evaluation set with 200 questions for each of Yes/No, Factoid, List, and Summary patterns
300 unlabeled PubMed introductions used for self-evolution pseudo-labeling

metrics: Factoid strict accuracy and lenient accuracy
Summary ROUGE-2 recall/F1 and ROUGE-SU4 recall/F1
baselines: Qwen3-8B in thinking and non-thinking modes
evaluation.setting: The extraction model was evaluated on BioOpenIE and zero-shot transferred to DDI, ChemProt, and BioRED without task-specific fine-tuning. Extraction matching used BERT sentence embeddings and cosine similarity threshold 0.85. For graph utility, AutoBioKG, AutoKG, EDC, and iText2KG were evaluated inside the same KG-RAG pipeline on filtered BioASQ Task 12b questions, with identical downstream retrieval and answer-generation procedures.

value: The self-evolved model improved over the seed model across DDI, ChemProt, BioRED, and BioOpenIE; reported F1 gains ranged from 1.88 to 3.64 percentage points.

In zero-shot relation extraction, AutoBioKG exceeded GPT-4o by 20.7 percentage points F1 on DDI, 19.7 on ChemProt, and 18.5 on BioRED; it exceeded the second-best baseline by more than 18% across all three datasets.
On BioASQ Yes/No questions, AutoBioKG achieved 80.5% accuracy and 75.9% macro-F1.
On BioASQ Factoid questions, AutoBioKG achieved 44.5% strict accuracy, reported as 8.0 percentage points above AutoKG and EDC.
On BioASQ List questions, AutoBioKG achieved 41.1% F-measure, reported as 15.9 percentage points above the second-best baseline, EDC.
For Summary questions, AutoBioKG had the highest ROUGE-2 recall, but EDC had slightly higher ROUGE-2 F1 (13.8% versus 13.5%).
The constructed BioASQ graph contained 3,507 nodes, 1,896 edges, average node degree 2.08, and 348 composite-triple edges, representing 18.35% of all relationships.

In BioOpenIE validation, a PhD-level computational biologist and Gemini3-pro achieved 94.2% inter-rater agreement, and the extraction pipeline achieved 87.1% accuracy against the consensus ground truth.

value: The method relies on a fixed composite-triple schema with one optional attribute slot for each entity and one condition slot on the relation, which may not express all biomedical event or n-ary structures.
The reported Summary evaluation did not dominate: EDC achieved higher ROUGE-2 F1 than AutoBioKG.
The self-evolution process was restricted to one refinement cycle because later cycles were observed to increase noise and produce diminishing returns.
Knowledge fusion depends on similarity thresholds and may retain novel entities or relations in unnormalized form when no sufficiently similar UMLS candidate exists.
The BioOpenIE annotation and validation pipeline is heavily LLM-mediated, so its quality depends on automated annotator behavior and the consensus procedure.

Review-level inference: comparison with baselines is strongest for the specified datasets and shared KG-RAG setup; it does not establish universal superiority across biomedical domains or graph-construction settings.

value: Context-dependent biomedical interactions remain difficult to represent when they require more complex structures than the composite triple schema.

The paper leaves open how to prevent hallucinated or semantically incorrect pseudo-labels during self-evolution; its ablation shows that supervised correction can propagate errors and confidence-only filtering admits noisy samples.
Entity and relation normalization remain incomplete for emerging terminology that falls below similarity thresholds or is absent from UMLS.
Generalization to patents, clinical trial reports, multimodal evidence, and broader biomedical document genres remains unresolved.
Review-level inference: reliable evaluation of context preservation, contradiction resolution, and mechanistic inference beyond the reported BioASQ case studies remains an open problem.
Review-level inference: the paper does not establish whether the graph remains accurate and consistent under continual updating at substantially larger corpus scale.
